walkthroughs.body_html:
Atmospheric Systems & Societies — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atmospheric Systems & Societies brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atmospheric Systems & Societies.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Decomposition.
Respiration.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: Why does renewable energy require energy storage solutions?
options: Renewable energy can never meet demand.
Decomposition.
Because they generate too much energy.
Solar and wind generation are intermittent - storage smooths out supply and demand.

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Because they generate too much energy.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
